requirements.requirement: node1 (dnsmasq) resolves the name app.internal to node2's private IP address
requirements.summary: UCI dhcp address record '/app.internal/10.100.101.11' added and committed on node1, dnsmasq restarted and confirmed bound on 10.100.101.10:53. node3's nslookup against node1 returns the correct address, and this was re-verified identically after node1's reboot.

requirements.requirement: node3 uses node1 as its DNS resolver (so app.internal resolves) without any local /etc/hosts entry
requirements.summary: node3's /etc/dhcpcd.conf was updated with a static domain_name_servers override pointing at node1 (10.100.101.10), dhcpcd restarted, and resolv.conf confirmed updated. /etc/hosts on node3 was checked and shown to contain no app.internal entry, both before and after node3's reboot.

requirements.requirement: node3 can reach node2's HTTP service on port 8080 by the name app.internal
requirements.summary: End-to-end curl from node3 to http://app.internal:8080/ succeeded, returning content served by node2, both immediately after configuration and after all three nodes were individually rebooted.

requirements.requirement: node2 actually runs the HTTP service on port 8080 (implicit precondition stated as fact in the task)
requirements.summary: Initial discovery showed nothing listening on 8080 on node2 (curl failed, empty proc/net/tcp). Executor installed python3 and created a persistent OpenRC service 'app-http' serving on 0.0.0.0:8080, enabled at boot, and verified listening via curl and the final listening-sockets snapshot. This is a reasonable prerequisite fix rather than scope creep, since the task's contract requires the service to be reachable.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on all three managed nodes with pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered state
requirements.summary: For each node, a pre-restart boot_id/uptime/service baseline was captured, a reboot was issued (with an initial failed attempt on node1 due to a missing nohup binary, corrected via a background subshell), and post-restart a differing boot_id plus healthy state (dnsmasq/UCI on node1, app-http service on node2, resolver/hosts/curl on node3) was directly observed. The fixed after_executor snapshot independently confirms new boot_ids for node2 and node3; for node1 the fixed snapshot's SSH-based boot-identity probe failed to connect at capture time, so that particular cross-check is unconfirmed, though the executor's own in-session probes directly show the boot_id change and recovery.

overall_summary: The executor correctly configured node1's dnsmasq to resolve app.internal to node2's IP and pointed node3's resolver at node1 without touching /etc/hosts, and directly verified end-to-end HTTP reachability by name both before and after rebooting all three nodes. It also discovered and fixed a real gap (node2's HTTP service was not actually running) as a necessary prerequisite. The mandatory restart protocol was completed for all three nodes with baseline, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered state, though the fixed after-executor snapshot could not independently confirm node1's new boot identity via SSH at capture time (a minor evidence gap, not a functional failure, since the executor's own probes show the transition).
limitations: The fixed after_executor global snapshot's SSH-based boot-identity check for node1 failed to connect (return_code 255), so the independent cross-check for node1's post-restart boot identity relies solely on executor-captured evidence rather than the fixed snapshot.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing executor commands map clearly to satisfying the task contract or the mandated restart protocol: UCI DNS record on node1, dhcpcd resolver override on node3, python3 install and app-http OpenRC service on node2 (a legitimate fix for the stated-but-absent HTTP service), and three individually acknowledged reboots. No unnecessary or abandoned mutations were found; the one failed reboot attempt on node1 (nohup missing) was a corrective retry rather than an unrelated experiment, and left no residue. Package-health diffs and a new /tmp/state/dnsmasqsec entry on node1, plus /tmp/reboot.log on node2/node3, are expected side effects of the dnsmasq restart and reboot cycle rather than executor-caused residue requiring cleanup.
